Console page to choose, configure and test a staff source before it runs
Scheduled sync with a dry run showing what would be added and removed
Each person's employment status and type read from the staff source and shown on People in words, with filters
Somebody the source says is suspended, has left or never activated, or whose employment type the install does not allow, cannot sign in or ask, and the administrator sees why on their page
Proved on the install: a reserved person suspended or of a type not allowed is refused sign-in and asking, and allowed again when the source or the setting says so

The staff sync gives each active person of an employment type the install allows a sign-in account, found by the source's identifier or work address before one is made and bound to their Brain person, and sends nobody anything: a person sets their password with Forgot password

An account the sync made is closed on the next sync when its person leaves, is suspended or is of a type no longer allowed, which disables their Brain person and ends their sessions; an account a person made is linked and never closed

Proved on the install: the staff sync makes an account for a reserved person with no email sent, Forgot password sets their password and then their second factor, and a reserved leaver's account is closed on the next sync

Departments come from the staff source or are managed on People, chosen on Settings; managed on People, the staff sync gives nobody a department, moves nobody, places nobody in a team or as a lead and offers no department to found, and a Starter pack follows the department People set

People moves several people to one department at once where departments are managed there, confirmed with everybody named, all of them or none, with the mover's authority over where each sits and where they go, and each move on the ledger under the mover

Proved on the install: with departments managed on People, reserved people moved together are in their new department, each move is on the ledger under the mover, and the next sync leaves them where they were put
Every capability a served route or console screen requires is in the capability registry an install is furnished with and can be granted from the console, and a sweep fails the build when one is not
A person marked as external cannot be saved without an end date, and on that date every grant, session and channel binding they hold stops working
A service account or API key acts at its named owner's live reach narrowed by its own declared limit, holds no grant of its own, and stops working the moment its owner loses that reach or leaves
A department head is granted audit reads over the people placed in their department, the staff sync rewrites that set when someone joins or leaves, and no audit entry records a department

The approve permission alone decides who may approve, and the console flags anyone holding the Approver role without an approve permission, or an approve permission without the role, as a misconfiguration

Identity is proved on an install: a person signs in through the company identity provider and receives a product id, binds a chat identity only with a single-use code minted in the web session, an unbound chat identity gets nothing and is told how to bind, the same person has the same reach on web and chat, a session ends at its idle and absolute limits, a password-only sign-in is refused administration, an account bound to nobody is told once who can link it, a forgotten password is reset by email, and the chosen staff source asserts only that people exist and is re-read on its schedule, with the checks recorded

The staff source credential given at setup is kept in the vault for the scheduled sync and replaced from the console, and a sync whose credential is refused changes nobody and says so on the staff sources screen
Appointing one person as both Super Admin and Connector Admin shows a separation-of-duties warning that must be acknowledged with a reason, and the acknowledgement is recorded in the audit trail
Every permissions requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves

When the staff sync marks a person as a leaver, every agent they own is stopped and listed for transfer on the console until a new owner accepts it, which starts it again at no wider reach than before and records the change of owner in the audit ledger (owner decision 2026-09-21: stop rather than keep running)
A record's access view, showing who can see that record, opens only for someone who can already see it

Every active person on the staff list is a Brain person the console lists, places and grants before their first sign-in, made by the staff sync without the sign-in service and found by their work address's digest, so a later sign-in binds to that person and never makes a second one

Sync now on Staff sources runs the staff sync at once for somebody who may connect a source, one run at a time and recorded like a scheduled run, and the page says when the last and next scheduled runs are and what the run did
Proved on the install: after a staff sync, every active person on the staff list is on People, and Sync now fills People without waiting for the scheduled run

A person made by hand is given their work email on their People page by somebody who may grant them, and the staff list's person for the same address is joined into them: automatically when that person has never signed in and holds nothing the sync did not write, after a confirmation otherwise, never when they sign in with their own account, and never by a matching name
Proved on the install: the first administrator adds their work email on their own People page and the person the staff list made for it is no longer listed

modules.name: The gate
leaf_texts: GateContext carrying trace id, principal, entitlements, hash, lane, channel, traffic class
Ordered middleware chain with explicit step boundaries
Recorder constructed at ingress before identify
Traffic class as a union with no default, so a new channel cannot compile without declaring it
Channel ingress normalisation to one internal event shape
Dedupe by unique index on channel and external id
Channel identity to principal resolution
Unrecognised identity path with no entitlement and a prompt to bind
Resolve entitlements from cache or database
Compute the entitlement hash
Channel capability intersection
Assurance-level intersection
Injection classifier over user input
Risk score written to the request row
Explicit no-block guarantee, tested
Autonomy tier escalation on a high score
Key from question, entitlement hash, agent config hash, policy epoch, source epochs
Lookup and store paths
Hit surfaced to the user with its age
Never-cache list for volatile question shapes
Lane classifier from features computable without a model
Agent selection: a named agent the person may use when they address one, an agent they may not use answering as one that does not exist, otherwise channel binding, then rules, then cheap classifier
Routing decision written to the row, never inferred afterwards
Project tools as agent grants intersected with entitlements
Static tool prefix with deferred loading so the provider cache is shared
Assert projection happens in our dispatcher, never delegated to a connector
Empty-catalogue error when a manifest declared required tools and none resolve
Agent loop invocation with the projected catalogue
Leash lookup for agent, target and scope
Shadow: simulate, record, return marked as simulated
Assisted: render artefact, suspend, await approval, resume
Autonomous: proceed, except a tool that declares a sensitive effect, which always waits for a person's approval of the exact prepared action
Three checks per call: capability, rung, mask
Invoke the redaction walker
Emit post-redaction payload to the trace sink only
Compose the answer with citations and freshness
Attach the trace reference for explainability
The entitlement resolver, the entitlement hash and the redactor take no agent as input, and a test fails if any of them is given one, so no agent setting can widen what a run returns
When more than one leash rule applies to an action the strictest rung wins, so a narrower rule can never loosen a broader one

A request passes identify, entitle, screen, lane classification and agent selection, cache, route and catalogue projection, in that order, before any model is called, and a test fails if a model call happens earlier in the chain or a step runs out of order

A person can address by name any agent they are allowed to use, in the web application and by mention in a chat channel, and the request goes to that agent instead of the router's choice, while an agent they may not use answers as one that does not exist

provider_health with live and probe ring buffers

Background prober on a sixty-second interval

Residency constraint attached to scope

Provider residency registry with documented storage location
Refusal path when no compliant rung exists

Another provider with an OpenAI-compatible interface is added from the console with only its address, key and model names, with no release
An agent uses a model level by default, and an administrator may pin a specific provider and model for it, tried first with the level's fallback behind it

modules.name: Knowledge, assets, document parsing
leaf_texts: Upload endpoint with size and type limits
Extract-from-link ingestion
Virus and content scanning before parse
Original storage in the object store with lifecycle policy
Ingestion queue with backpressure
Docling integration for layout-aware extraction
Table extraction preserved through chunking
Tika fallback for unsupported formats
OCR path for scanned documents
Parse failure handling with a visible error naming the cause
Memory-bounded parse worker with a hard container limit
Chunking strategy with overlap and size bounds
Chunk metadata carrying document, scope, owner and position
Local embedding via Qwen3 through the inference server
Batch embedding with a queue
Re-embedding on model change with a rebuild command
knowledge table: content, scope, owner, verified_by, verified_at, review_by, state
Company, department and personal visibility levels
Publishing flow: uploading never widens scope
Promotion to company scope requires the gated path
Supersession: a newer version marks the older superseded
Scheduled job opening re-verification tasks from review_by
Verification badge surfaced in the answer
Column classification for tabular knowledge such as price lists
Sell price visible while cost and margin are restricted
Classification editor in the console

Every knowledge item carries exactly one kind from a closed list (SOP, policy, FAQ, pricing note, service information, service package, brand guidelines, company rule, best practice, template, training material, approved solution), set when it is added, shown in the library and usable to narrow what an answer or an agent retrieves, and a pricing note never holds the price rows themselves
A solution becomes company knowledge only after a named person approves it, and the item records what it solved, who approved it and when, and is retrieved like any other verified item

A plain text, Markdown, PDF or Word document can be added from the console and answered from on an install with no worker, object store or embedding server, and it is found by text search within the uploader's scope
A retrieved passage carries the department, visibility and owner its item was stored with, so a knowledge grant over one department reads that department's passages and never another's
Every knowledge collection, connected source and agent names a steward, set and changed in the console, and the steward is the person notified when anyone grants themselves access to that object
A price list is held as classified table rows, and a price list uploaded as a document is offered for conversion to those rows rather than indexed as text

The embedding width is an install setting read by the migration, a width above what the vector index supports is refused when it is read, and changing the width is refused while any chunk holds a vector
Marking a knowledge item public is allowed to a super admin, or to a department admin for their own department's items only, and each marking writes a ledger entry naming the person

The knowledge lifecycle is proved on an install: an administrator uploads a document holding a table and adds a link, sets its kind, owner and review date, a question is answered citing the passage with its freshness and verification badge, a newer version supersedes the older, and a due review date opens a re-verification task, with the checks recorded
Every knowledge requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves

Every stored vector records the model that produced it, changing the embedding model rebuilds every chunk in the background while answers keep using the previous vectors, and a search never compares vectors from two models

Every stored chunk records which parser produced it, and a citation to a passage recognised by OCR or read by the text fallback says so, including for the OCR pages of an otherwise layout-read document
An OCR confidence floor is applied per page, and a page under it is kept out of the index with a visible parse notice naming the page while the document's legible pages are indexed

The largest upload the install accepts is parsed by the layout service within its container limit, and the worker reports at start when the declared upload limit exceeds what the parse service can accept (needs the owner's choice of upload limit, container size or request format)

Microsoft Teams adapter

Telegram adapter
Web widget with session minting and abuse guard
Email adapter, inbound and outbound
REST API with key management
Every channel adapter delivers its planned message through the vendor's API using a credential held outside configuration, and a delivery the vendor refused is recorded as refused and never as sent
A WhatsApp webhook is accepted only when its signature matches the app secret over the exact bytes received, and an unsigned or altered request is refused before it is read

Each channel is configured on the install as its own record holding its tenant identifiers, secret slot and on or off state, and switching one off stops both receiving and sending on it without touching any other channel
An approval is decided only in the console, the staff web application or on a Lark card; a reply on WhatsApp, email or any other channel never decides one, and the approver is told where to decide it

An anonymous website widget visitor holds one grant over knowledge an administrator marked public and nothing else, a question about anything else is answered as nothing found, marking or unmarking an item public is audited with who did it, and a department admin can mark only their own department's knowledge public

Every shipped channel is proved on an install: on each chat channel, by email, through the REST API and in the web application a bound person asks and gets a permission-correct answer through that channel's own credential with progress streamed, a sender bound to nobody learns nothing about the company, a message whose signature does not verify is refused unread, a platform retry produces one answer, a waiting approval notice reaches the person it names, the conversation continues on a second channel, and an agent not enabled on a channel refuses there, with the checks recorded

Group chat and channel policy are proved on an install: in one group chat people with different reach see a shared message at the floor of everyone present and each receives their own body privately or as a link where the gate re-runs, a channel whose policy excludes a sensitivity class refuses to carry it, and an approval card is offered only where approvals are allowed, with the checks recorded

The website widget is proved on an install: an anonymous visitor on a website is answered only from knowledge marked public, a question about anything else returns nothing found, and repeated requests from one origin are capped and the session expires sooner than a signed-in one, with the checks recorded

The website widget's answer is written by the model from the passages an administrator marked public and from nothing else, with those passages shown beside it, when the owner has switched model answers on; with the switch off, or when the model cannot answer, the visitor is given the passages themselves

What the website widget's model answers may cost a day is a figure the owner sets on the Rate limits screen, each answer's cost is counted from the spend ledger under the widget's own name, and once the day's figure is used up the widget answers with the passages until midnight UTC

Proved on the install: with model answers switched on and a cap, a visitor's question is answered by the model from the public passage alone, the cost is on the spend ledger under the widget, and the answer after the cap is used up is the passages

MCP transport adapter
REST and OpenAPI transport adapter driven by a spec plus field mapping
Database transport adapter restricted to allowlisted read-only views
Custom code transport adapter running sandboxed
Connector registration, enable, disable, upgrade
Manifest hash pinning so a silent redefinition fails closed on reconnect
Credential reference model, never a value in configuration
OpenBao storage with per-run leases
Scope-at-connect: one folder or one pipeline rather than everything
Read-only by default with write as a separate deliberate grant
Identity mode per tool: requester credentials by default, service credentials declared
Rotation without redeploy
Per-connector token bucket
Circuit breaker per connector
Retry policy with backoff and jitter
Metrics: requests per second and minute, concurrency, 429 rate, latency, error rate
Configured ceilings per source, matching documented limits
proj.record table with source, entity type, identifiers and hot fields
Twelve-field cap per entity kind enforced by the manifest validator
Five-clause projectability test enforced at manifest review
PII deny-list blocking email, phone, address, identity numbers, bank and salary
Visibility predicate stored, never a resolved ACL
Change-signal subscription: webhook, CDC or updated-since cursor
No change signal means no projected fields, enforced
Backfill job with rate-limit awareness
Staleness surfaced in the answer
Live fetch path with an eight-hundred-millisecond timeout
Parallel fan-out across independent sources with one critical path
Global and per-source call budgets
Thundering-herd protection on cache miss

An answer names a source that could not be fetched only to an asker who could already see that source, anyone else is told part of the answer is unavailable, and the full list goes to the operator log
Laravel MySQL via read-only views
Freshdesk
Lark Base
Lark Wiki
Xero
HubSpot
Google Drive or Microsoft 365
Google Analytics is a connector that reads one property's traffic and conversion figures for a named date range, read-only, and an agent without that property bound gets nothing from it
Search Console is a connector that reads one verified site's queries, pages, clicks, impressions and indexing issues for a named date range, read-only
Cloudflare is a connector that reads the zones, DNS records and security events of the accounts it was given, and any DNS change goes through a prepared action a person approves
A domain and hosting connector reports each client domain's registrar, expiry date and hosting status, so an expiry question is answered from the source rather than from a spreadsheet
Slack is a connector that reads only the channels it was invited to, and a message from a channel the asker cannot see in Slack is never returned to them

Google Workspace is a connector whose included services (mail, calendar, documents) are chosen at connect, and mail and calendar are read with the asking person's own authorisation rather than a company-wide key
Every shipped connector can be connected, configured and switched off from the console, including the visibility rule and department it needs, so no source has to be connected at the server

An administrator adds a connector for a new API from the console by supplying its specification, field mapping and credential reference, and it becomes available to agents after review without a release
Manifest review refuses a projected field that is not an id, join key, status value, timestamp, visibility predicate or a display label of at most 120 characters

A canary value placed in a federated field of a recorded source response is found in no table, memory row, projection row or log after the answer is delivered, apart from the payload store within its retention

Live reading is proved on an install: a question over a connected ticket source is answered live, a canary value from a ticket body is afterwards found in no table, memory, projection or log, deny-listed fields never appear in the projection, a question spanning many records is answered from projected headers, and document embeddings are computed with no outbound call, with the checks recorded
A change signal from a source advances that source's epoch, so a cached answer that read the source is never served after the source changed

A connector declares each write it can perform as a tool with a side-effect class, connecting it shows every such write switched off until an administrator turns one on with the change audited, and a write that is on runs only as a prepared action a person approved, at the requester's reach, reported done only after it is read back from the source

A connector that authorises by OAuth completes the consent flow from the console, keeps the refresh token by reference in the vault, and renews access before it expires without a person, and a refresh or consent the vendor refuses marks the source down on connector health in words

A scheduled check reads each connected source's schema every night, and a renamed or removed field a tool depends on is shown on connector health and makes that tool answer as degraded rather than silently return nothing

Live connector answers are proved on an install: each shipped connector is connected from the console with its key in the vault and scoped to the slice it was given, a question about a client's open tickets is answered from the live source citing the record, field and time read, and a call to a connector not bound to the agent is refused even though the asker could reach it, with the checks recorded

Connector safety is proved on an install: a key written in the console is never shown back in any screen, response or log, is leased for one run and revoked at its end, and is rotated without a redeploy; a source pushed past its rate ceiling is throttled and its circuit opens; and a changed tool manifest or renamed source field is shown on connector health rather than silently answered, with the checks recorded

A connector write is proved on an install: a write that was off is turned on by an administrator, the agent prepares a reply to a ticket, a person approves it, it runs once at the requester's reach and is reported done only after it is read back from the source, and a signed outbound event is delivered to a receiving system with a retry after a refused first attempt, with the checks recorded

A record the source has deleted is detected by the sync, withheld from answers from the next completed read and recorded with when it was noticed, and a record the source later returns is served again without reviving the retired row

The ticket desk connector can post a reply to a ticket as a prepared action, sent only after a person approves it and reported done only after it is read back from the ticket desk, as the first connector write of the first complete maintenance agent
Every connectors requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves

A connector keeps only a minimal index of a source (identifiers, display names and the few fields needed to find a record), never a copy of business values, and a test fails if the projection holds a field outside that minimal set
Every value an answer or an agent uses from a connected source is read live from the source at that moment, at the asker's reach

run_skill_script as the single execution tool, sandboxed and leashed
SOP import accepting messy Word and Confluence documents
An administrator exports an approved skill as a package another install can import, carrying its version and digest, and the import on the other side still lands unreviewed
An administrator edits a skill in the console and the edit is saved as a new version that waits for review, while every agent keeps the version it was pinned to until somebody moves it
A skill declares the knowledge it needs, and assigning it to an agent whose knowledge scope does not cover that need is refused with what is missing
A skill carries example tasks with the behaviour expected of it, and a new version cannot be approved until those examples have been rehearsed against it

An agent produces a document, a slide deck or a spreadsheet from an approved company template through one registered generation tool, and the file is stored as an artifact holding only what the caller may see
An agent reads a file a person attached to the conversation through a registered tool at that person's reach, and cannot read a file somebody else attached

An external AI service other than a chat model, such as image generation or speech to text, is registered as a tool with a required capability and a side-effect class, and is refused to any agent whose ceiling does not name it

Every tool that sends a message to a client, issues a quotation, changes DNS or hosting, changes financial records, deletes information, publishes content or changes a production system declares that effect, and no leash entry or promotion lets such a call run before a person approves the exact prepared action

Each sensitive action the owner named (sending a client email, issuing a quotation, changing DNS, recording a financial change, deleting a record, publishing content, changing a production system) has a registered tool that performs it only after approval of the exact prepared action

Human approval of sensitive actions is proved on an install: for each named sensitive effect an agent prepares the action, the approver sees the real artefact at their own reach in the console and on a Lark card, the action runs once only after approval, an irreversible one needs two approvers neither of whom asked for it, a rejected one never runs, a reply by WhatsApp or email decides nothing, and no leash promotion lets such an action run unapproved, with the checks recorded

An administrator can switch off one tool from the console, after which every call to it from any agent, workflow or automation is refused naming the switch until it is switched back on, and a department admin can stop their own department the same way

An agent checks whether a website is working through a registered read-only HTTP tool that reports status, redirects, certificate expiry and response time for an address within its ceiling, and opens the read-only browser only when a rendered page must be inspected

An agent can run code in a sandbox with no network and no credentials over files and results the caller may see, the call is leashed and recorded, and its output is redacted like any other tool result
An administrator may approve a skill they imported themselves and the approval is recorded as a self-approval the audit view can list, while an import by anyone else needs a different reviewer

An install is furnished with a starter skill library holding an SEO audit, keyword research, website health check, ticket analysis, complaint analysis, monthly SEO report, proposal generation and website troubleshooting skill, each approved, assignable and rehearsed against its example tasks

The tool catalogue is proved on an install: one agent calls a typed API tool, a pinned third-party tool server, the sandboxed code tool, a document generation tool whose file is stored as an artifact with its provenance and retention class, and a file a person attached, each running as the requesting person, while a tool not attached to it, a tool switched off for the install and a tool whose manifest changed are each refused, with the checks recorded

The skill lifecycle is proved on an install: a skill is created in the console and another imported from a repository at a pinned commit, neither runs until reviewed against a diff, a self-approval of an own import is recorded as one, an edit becomes a new version that waits for review while agents keep their pinned version, approval waits for its example tasks to be rehearsed, and an exported skill lands unreviewed on a second install, with the checks recorded

Skill reuse is proved on an install: one approved skill is assigned to two agents and changes what both runs do, the agents load it by name first and in full only on demand, its script runs only through the sandboxed execution tool, an assignment whose knowledge or tool needs exceed the agent's scope is refused with what is missing, and removing it from one agent leaves it on the other with the detachment in history, with the checks recorded
A skill's approval digest covers the bytes of every script it carries, so a script changed after approval is refused before it runs
Skill frontmatter validation refuses a description that does not begin by saying when the skill should be used
A skill carries one or more categories an administrator sets, and the skills screen offers them as filter chips drawn only from skills the reader may see

A person creates a skill by describing it in conversation, the system drafts the skill with its instructions, needed knowledge, tools and example tasks, and the draft lands unreviewed and not executable, exactly like an import
Every tools requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves
A skill's digest covers the bytes of every script it carries, so a skill with scripts is admitted and changing one byte of a script requires a new review

Every way work reaches an agent (web, channel, automation, workflow step, delegated subtask) enters the same agent runtime, and a test fails if a second code path calls a model with tools
An agent run stops after a bounded number of model turns and tool calls, and the stop is recorded on the run with the bound that was reached
An administrator can halt one agent, and every run of that agent, including its automations and delegated subtasks, is refused until the halt is lifted

An agent answers only on the channels an administrator enabled for it, and a message reaching it from any other channel is refused before the agent runs, in the same words as an agent that does not exist
A question that reaches an agent through any channel is answered at the intersection of the asker's reach and that agent's ceiling, never at the wider of the two
An approved action runs once without the requester returning, at the requester's reach re-resolved at that moment, and a rejected, amended or lapsed one never runs

A suspended action with an irreversible effect runs only after two different people have approved the same prepared action, neither of them the person who asked for it nor the principal it runs as, and the database refuses it as well as the route
An agent run can call only the connectors bound to that agent, and a call to any other connector is refused by the gate even when the asking person could reach that source directly

A maintenance agent template ships in the catalogue declaring a ticket desk and a maintenance records source, maintenance skills, the HTTP website check tool and the read-only browser tool, and it installs into an agent that answers (needs-rupash 170 A: workflows, memory, channels and the documents it reads are set where the builder links to, not in the template)

An agent's connector list compiles into its ceiling as the tools those connectors provide, the gate resolves it through the one intersection used for every ceiling entry, and a test fails if connector access is decided anywhere else
A run that outlives a grant it started with is re-judged at its next tool call, so an automation or a streamed answer stops using a capability from the moment it lapses or is revoked

The harness is proved on an install: a question through each of the fast, answer and task lanes, a task killed mid-run and resumed, a halted agent, a switched-off tool, a run that hits its turn bound, a person addressing a named agent and an injected tool result are each exercised, and each trace shows the lane, the gate order, the projected catalogue, leased credentials never exposed and the refusal reason, with the checks recorded

Only a super admin can publish or retire an agent at company-wide visibility; a department admin or member who tries is refused, and a published company-wide agent appears for a person in every department
A department admin installs an agent from the catalogue on the install and it answers its golden set correctly, with the time from choosing the template to the first correct answer recorded

The maintenance workflow is put on the installed maintenance agent from the Automations page, which the builder links to, and the agent runs it (needs-rupash 170 A: a workflow is not part of the template)

The SEO agent template declares the analytics and search console connectors and SEO skills, and installs into an agent that answers; the monthly SEO report workflow and the chat and web channels are set where the builder links to (needs-rupash 170 A: workflows, memory, channels and the documents it reads are set where the builder links to, not in the template)

The catalogue has a sales, a finance, a support and a project management agent template, each declaring its connectors and skills and installing into an agent that answers (needs-rupash 170 A: workflows, memory, channels and the documents it reads are set where the builder links to, not in the template)

The agent lifecycle is proved on an install: a template with a missing connector installs pinned to Shadow with its badge, a custom agent is composed, rehearsed as a named person and published through the canaries and a second approver, an upgrade is offered and declined, a personal agent stays invisible to others, and an agent is saved as a private template, with the checks recorded

An install mints its template signing key once at setup into the vault, the application reads it and nothing can replace it while a signed template version exists, and the built-in templates are signed with it when the install is furnished

Accepting a new template version runs the same binding and completeness checks as installing it, so a tool the version declares is bound to a registered tool or reported missing, and a newly required connector or placeholder reopens the wizard before the version runs
Every agents requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves
A leash rung can carry an end date, the gate keeps the rung until that date and then reports it due for review rather than loosening it silently, and the Leash screen shows when each pinned rung ends
Every harness requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves

A template authored from an existing agent is stored as a draft that survives a restart, is shown for review with every value hoisted out of it, and becomes installable only after a person publishes it
An agent's audience can list named people and several departments, and adding one lets them find the agent without widening what any run reaches.
The manifest has a settable overview path, older signed templates still verify under their own schema version, and no model prompt includes the overview.
On an install with no vault the template catalogue says installing is unavailable and no signing key is stored anywhere else.
An agent's audience can name several departments and individual people beside its level, and each added person or department gains discovery only, never reach

A super admin creates an agent for the whole company from the console, from a template or from scratch, and in one flow sets its skills, tools, connectors and which actions need approval, and is linked from there to where its workflows, documents, memory and channels are set (needs-rupash 170 A)
A department admin creates an agent for their own department in the same flow, and can choose only the skills, tools, connectors and knowledge their department holds

On the install a super admin and a department admin each create an agent from their requirements, assign its skills and tools, and the agent answers through its channel, with the checks recorded (the workflow and the channel are set where the builder links to, needs-rupash 170 A)
A template agent installs with one click using sensible defaults, and the full setup wizard stays available for anyone who wants to change them

modules.name: Memory and learning
leaf_texts: Session memory in Valkey with thread lifetime
Persistent memory table with scope and capability tags
Adaptive memory table with confidence and decay
Capability set recorded at formation and re-checked at read
Never authoritative over the database, asserted by test
Question re-asked in different words within a window
Answer copied
Contradicting follow-up
Escalation to a human
Human takeover of an Assisted action
Ticket reopened within a window
Approval rejected with a reason
All signals logged from the first migration
Tier zero: session, silent

Tier one automatic for one person only: that person's preferences and entity links corroborated by a hard identifier, while a helpful or unhelpful mark and negative signals are counted and never demote or boost anything by themselves
Tier two shadow then review: fast-path rules and procedural shortcuts are computed in shadow beside the real answer and offered to a named reviewer with their evidence, never promoted by themselves
Tier two agreement threshold that makes a shadow rule eligible for review, with no job that puts a rule into effect without a person's approval
Tier three gated: scope widening, company knowledge, leash increase, money-boundary merge, capability addition
Blast-radius classifier deciding the tier automatically
Time decay reducing confidence below the retrieval threshold
Supersession on contradiction, marked rather than deleted
Source truth wins immediately, memory demoted and flagged
Entitlement expiry: memories stop matching when capabilities change
Weekly digest of tier one and two learning with one-click undo
Per-agent memory tab listing what was learned, the evidence, the confidence and a delete control
Department admin view of department memory
Tier three review queue with a budget alarm when it grows

The context a model is shown for one turn is assembled in one place from the conversation, the task, the project, the memories about the asker, the agent's memory and company knowledge, each read at the asker's reach at that moment, and the trace names which parts were included and which were left out

A question about a client project is answered with the current context of that project, its client, open tickets and recent decisions, read from the sources at the asker's reach on every turn and never stored as a memory
A model answering a question is shown the memories the asker may still recall about themselves, marked as hints, and the answer never cites a memory as its source

A person can mark an answer helpful or unhelpful with one action in the console and in every channel, and the mark is stored against the answer's trace reference with no free text and counted as a learning signal

A person correcting an answer may give the right answer in their own words, and it is held as a learning candidate under the permissions of the conversation, changing no knowledge, rule or memory until a person who owns the affected knowledge approves it

A learning candidate a reviewer approves is applied exactly once as the knowledge item, rule, skill revision or grant it proposed, the ledger records who approved it, and a rejected candidate keeps its reason and is not proposed again from the same evidence
An output a person approved without changes is recorded as a positive example for the agent and skill that produced it, and it influences later runs only through the tier its change would reach

An administrator can set how long inferred memories last and how many independent agreements make a learned rule eligible for review, within bounds the product fixes, and no setting can move a kind of change to a lower oversight tier

Every change learning applies to an agent is marked machine-authored in that agent's per-field ownership, so a person can list and revert exactly what the agent taught itself apart from what an administrator set
A memory that is used and confirmed again regains its confidence, and one that is not falls below the retrieval threshold on the configured schedule while its audit record stays

A learned rule or shortcut that has agreed with real answers in shadow is offered to a named reviewer with its evidence and takes effect only after that person approves it, and the approval is recorded

A helpful or unhelpful mark is counted against its trace and reported, and by itself changes no retrieval ranking, memory, rule, knowledge or agent setting, and a test fails if a mark alone alters what a later answer retrieves

A memory is formed only from the kinds of observation the product lists (a preference, an entity link, a procedure, a correction held for review), and a value read from a connected source is never stored as a memory or learned rule, proved by a canary value read during a conversation that appears in no memory or rule row afterwards, and an agent whose memory switch is off forms none
Corrections that repeat the same fix across conversations are grouped into one learning candidate that carries every instance as evidence, rather than one candidate each

Memory and context are proved on an install: session memory ends with its thread, a preference applies only to its owner, project context reflects a source change on the next turn, a memory that contradicts the source is demoted, removing an entitlement stops replay, a person reads, edits and deletes memory about themselves and it leaves retrieval at once, and the trace names the context kinds used and left out, with the checks recorded

The learning loop is proved on an install: an unhelpful mark changes nothing, a correction carrying the right answer is held as a protected candidate, repeated corrections form one candidate, a reviewer approves it and it is applied once, the digest lists it with undo, and a failed workflow step and an evaluation each open a candidate while an unanswered question appears as a knowledge gap, with the checks recorded
Every learning requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves
A stated memory is recalled at the confidence it was formed with however old it is, only inferred and session memories decay, and every memory kind declares which it is
Every memory requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves

A person whose every grant is scoped to their department recalls the memories formed from their own conversations, in answers and on the Memory screen, proved with a reader holding no company-wide grant
Pausing learning on one agent stops memory formation and learning proposals from that agent's runs, and the pause can only narrow what is learned.
Promoting a tier-two rule and deciding a tier-three item from the console records who agreed and takes effect on the next run.

leaf_texts: Job table with state machine, attempts, and scheduling
Procrastinate integration on Postgres
Worker pool with per-class concurrency
Cancellation and timeout
Dead-letter handling with an operator surface
LangGraph checkpointer on Postgres
Our own re-drive driver for crash recovery
Checkpoint at every side-effect boundary
Resume after restart with state intact
Entitlement re-check at every resume point
Idempotency key on every side-effecting operation
Operation state machine: pending, sent, unknown, verifying, succeeded, failed
Verification read-back per connector
Connectors without read-back restricted to read-only, declared in the manifest
Kill-after-side-effect test proving exactly-once
Trigger types: schedule, connector event, webhook
Automations start from named outcome templates, while workflows are authored in the console as stored, versioned step data rather than drawn on a blank canvas
Automation principal resolving the owner's live entitlements at each run
Suspension when the owner loses a required entitlement
Timeout and expiry on every approval step
Run history with cost per run
Postgres outbox with retry and backoff
Signing and delivery guarantees
Subscriber management in the console
An administrator can define a multi-step workflow from the console as stored, versioned data, and an agent assigned that workflow runs it without a person performing each step
A workflow step can call a skill, read a connector or use a tool, and every such step runs through the gate at the run's reach, the leash and the meter, exactly as an agent's own call does
A workflow step's output is named and schema-checked, and a later step can read only outputs that earlier steps declared
A workflow step can run only when a condition over earlier named outputs holds, and a skipped step is recorded as skipped with the condition that decided it
Workflow steps declared parallel start together, and the step that combines them runs only after each has finished or been recorded as a gap
Each workflow step carries its own retry limit and backoff, a side-effecting step is retried only through its idempotency key, and a step that exhausts its retries takes its declared failure path

Every finished workflow or automation run emits a success or failure signal naming the workflow, the agent and the step that failed, and repeated failures of one step open a learning candidate instead of changing the workflow
A workflow that reads two connectors, calls two skills, waits for an approval and delivers a document runs end to end on the install and leaves one trace a person can follow

The monthly search report workflow runs on the install for a named client: it resolves the client, reads the period's analytics and search console figures, finds the previous report, runs the search checks, writes recommendations into the report template, holds it for approval and delivers it, and no step but the approval is performed by a person, with the run recorded

A scheduler inside the application runs every registered scheduled control when it is due, holding a database lock so two application copies never run the same one, and a control with no run inside its window raises an alert

Automations are proved on an install: a scheduled, a connector-event and a webhook automation each run as their owner from a named template, one is suspended when its owner loses a required access and offered for adoption when the owner leaves, run history shows cost and outcome, and where the optional canvas is enabled it reaches the platform only over the internal network, with the checks recorded

Workflow control flow is proved on an install: a workflow with two parallel skill steps, a conditional step that is skipped, a step that fails, retries through its idempotency key and takes its failure path, and a combining step that records the gap shows every outcome in its one trace, with the checks recorded

The automation gallery ships a daily brief, capture of deals from group chats into the customer records held as drafts, and drafted email replies a person sends, each declaring its trigger, connectors and approval step

Every notice the product composes is delivered to the person it names through their bound channel or the configured email relay, and a notice that could not be delivered is shown as undelivered on the notifications screen
An agent runs only the workflows assigned to it, and a request that would start any other workflow through it is refused before the first step runs
Every human approval requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves

modules.name: Multi-agent execution
leaf_texts: Planner proposing subtasks and data dependencies
Subtask contract: objective, output schema, tool hints, scope predicate
Schema validation on every subtask result, failure rather than merge input
Prose explicitly disallowed as a subtask contract
Dependency graph with cost and coupling weights
Six arithmetic conditions evaluated before any child starts
Collapse to a single loop as the default when any condition fails
Gate inputs and verdict recorded for audit
Child grant computed in SQL as parent intersect agent intersect subtask
Database trigger rejecting any non-subset delegation row
Orchestrator has no grant verb, asserted
Depth cap of two and per-run concurrency cap of eight
Global parallelism budget across all runs
Merge step writing the final answer from validated inputs
Per-subtask cost and duration surfaced to the user
Partial-failure handling with a stated gap
A coordinating agent can hand a subtask only to agents an administrator allowed it to call, and a call to any other agent is refused before the child starts
A specialist agent handed a subtask reads through its own knowledge, skills and connectors within the asker's reach, and the coordinator receives only the specialist's schema-checked result
A planner step asks a model for subtasks and their dependencies, and its proposal passes the existing proposal checks before any child runs

A request to analyse a client's website and prepare an improvement proposal runs on the install as a coordinating agent handing website, search data, competitor and services and pricing subtasks to specialist agents along administrator-set links, in parallel where independent, each at the asker's reach intersected with its own ceiling, and merging their checked results into one proposal whose single trace shows each child's reach, result, cost and the fan-out verdict, with the checks recorded
An agent spawns parallel subtasks or workers only when fan-out is enabled on it by its department admin, and a run of an agent without it runs as a single loop with the reason recorded
The cost check may run a coordinator's specialist agents one after another, but never replaces a specialist's work with the coordinator's own

modules.name: Browser and computer use
leaf_texts: Ephemeral gVisor container per run
Playwright for Python with Chromium
Worker owning the CDP session and snapshot serialisation
Accessibility-tree snapshots rather than screenshots
tmpfs-only writable layer, destroyed at run end, never reused
Per-run network namespace
Planner that never reads page content, asserted by test
Envelope compilation: plan intersected with capabilities and skill ceiling
Envelope storage and approval record
Target registry with declared surface maps
Enforcer with policy compiled at container start and immutable after
Reference validation against the snapshot just produced
Origin allowlist check per action
Write verb and count checks against the envelope
mitmproxy sidecar as the sole route out
Second independent check in the control plane on every returned result
Placeholder resolution at the tool-execution boundary
Origin binding so a secret only substitutes on its own domain
TOTP generation server-side from a stored seed
Outbound scrubbing from message history
Vision disabled so a credential cannot be read off a screenshot
Rubric generated from the goal before seeing the trajectory
Two-pass scoring: actions only, then with screenshots
Agent's own success claim ignored
Tuned for low false-positive rate, accepting false negatives
Out-of-band read-back from the system of record where possible
Global browser concurrency limit
Per-domain concurrency limit
Per-agent limit
Memory and CPU caps per session
Global kill switch
Full session recording with retention policy
Skill loader refusing a browser skill where an API tool exists, unless exempted with a named approver and expiry
Read-only capability shipped first
Write capability behind envelope approval
Assisted ceiling on writes unless a per-surface exception is signed

An agent can operate an allowlisted desktop application inside an isolated virtual desktop, with every action recorded, every write held for a person's approval, and no route to any other application or network
A browser action outside its approved envelope suspends the run and sends a new approval naming the breach, and actions inside the envelope never ask again

Browser approval is proved on an install: a read-only website check runs without approval, a planned browser write is shown once as a readable diff of its envelope and approved, steps inside the envelope are not asked again, and a step outside it suspends the run and asks again, with the checks recorded
A browser run starts from an empty profile in its own container and cannot attach to or import a staff member's browser profile, cookies or session, asserted by a test

Website and portal reading is proved on an install: asked whether a live website is working, an agent checks it over HTTP, opens the rendered page in the read-only browser from an empty sandboxed profile with egress limited to that origin, and cites what it observed; and a read-only browser task logs in to a portal with no API using a vault credential the model never sees and returns the figure asked for; the session recording is kept under its retention class and the checks are recorded

A browser write is proved on an install: one multi-step form-filling task against a registered target runs at the Assisted rung only after its plan is approved, a step outside the approved plan is refused, and the task is reported done only after an independent read-back from the target system, with the checks recorded
The browser sandbox runs on an install, and an agent whose ceiling holds the browser tools opens a page in it.

An administrator grants a per-surface browser write exception or a browser-over-API exemption from the console with an approver and expiry, it is recorded in the audit ledger as a leash change, listed until it lapses, and a run compiled after expiry no longer has it

On the install a browser run's outcome is scored by a judge from its actions and admitted frames against the rubric fixed before the run, and a declared target's result is read back from its system of record before the run is reported done
On the install open browser sessions are counted as they start and end, and a session over the global, per-website or per-agent limit waits or is refused with a sentence naming the limit

On the install an agent's browser write to an allowlisted site is compiled into an envelope, approved by a person, signs in with a vaulted credential that never appears in the plan, trace or recording, and performs exactly the approved writes
Browser session recordings on the install are written to the object store at run end, and a scheduled job removes expired ones, keeps held ones and reports undated objects

modules.name: Verz Studio, the builder
leaf_texts: Composer sections: identity, persona, knowledge scope, skills, tools, connectors, leash, tests, each a reference to a separately created part, and links to where workflows, documents, memory and channels are set (needs-rupash 170 A)
Forms generated from the manifest JSON Schema via react-jsonschema-form
AI co-author proposing accept or reject diffs
Draft, save and version handling
Everything re-derived server-side, so an authored list is intent not authorisation
Read-only trace graph over completed runs using React Flow
Bounded procedure canvas outputting a SKILL.md
Five node kinds with scope predicates as the only conditional grammar
No code node, enforced
Run against the real gate, leash and redactor
Cassette replay so no real side effect fires
Per-persona rehearsal showing what each user would see
Measured cost per run from the rehearsal
System-authored permission canaries that can block
Author-written tests advisory forever
Grant-widening demotes to Shadow and requires a second approver
Instruction edits publish without demotion
Router collision check
Publish record with who, when and the diff

An agent, skill or knowledge item published at department reach waits for that department's admin and one published company-wide waits for a Super Admin, and a department admin can neither approve a publication outside their department nor widen an item to the whole company alone
Publishing an agent whose median rehearsed run costs more than its department's per-run ceiling is held until the department admin approves it, and the publish record shows the measured cost

A person describes an agent in conversation and the system drafts its persona, knowledge, skills, connectors, channels and workflows as a saved draft within the person's ceiling, which then goes through rehearsal and publish like any other draft

M20.5.1.why: Built: a department's administrator can no longer publish an agent to the whole company or approve a knowledge item to it alone; that needs the authority held over everything, and for a department it needs the authority held in that department. The skill library is one company-wide object, so only the authority over everything decides about a skill. The publications queue offers each administrator only the requests they could decide. To prove it on the install: after the release, open Install, Acceptance, run the checks and read the row 'a department admin decides only for their department', which should pass in the two newest runs.

M20.5.2.why: Built: behind the switch 'Hold an agent that costs more than its department allows' (ships off), publishing an agent to a department whose per-run ceiling is below what one run costs waits for that department's administrator, tells the author both figures in the install's currency, and the publish record carries the cost of each version. Not what the leaf says in two ways: the figure is the run's price from the product's own estimator (the same one the pre-flight uses) and not the median of rehearsed runs, because rehearsals record no cost yet (needs-you question); and no screen writes a department's per-run ceiling yet (M21.1.2), so on an install the hold fires only for a ceiling written some other way. The check 'a costly publish waits for a colleague in the department' proves the hold over a ceiling it writes itself.

The install's own check a_short_peak_run_is_driven_judged_and_kept_and_leaves_nothing proves the machinery in a rolled-back transaction with no model called, and closes the leaf when the install's two newest runs both pass it. The peak run itself is the owner's decision (needs-rupash 194; item 103 says CI, not the install). Install proof, steps: (1) open the Install page's list of checks after a deploy and see that check pass; (2) only if you choose to run the peak: turn on the Features page switch for the load test, make a department called load_test with two people and a small document only it can read, then follow docs/install/scaling.md, The peak load test.
