modules.name: Joiner, mover, leaver
leaf_texts: Provisioning from the identity provider
Role and starter capability pack assignment
Department assignment with scope
Welcome path with three department-scoped starter questions
Entitlement re-resolution on the next request
Personal agents following the person
Delegations re-evaluated and suspended rather than narrowed
Cached answers unreachable by construction
Memories tagged with the old capability set no longer replayed
Knowledge access changing with no reindex
Test covering every one of the above
Immediate disable with session termination
Owned agents flagged for adoption
Automations suspended
Personal knowledge and memory disposition policy
Audit record retained regardless

Joiner, mover and leaver handling is proved on an install: a person moved between departments loses the old department's knowledge, agents, cached answers and memories on their next request and gains the new ones with no reindex, purge or restart, a delegation that now exceeds their reach is suspended, a leaver's agents pass to the department admin, an item they own but can no longer reach leaves their workspace, a run in progress stops using a revoked grant at its next step, and an external person and a service key stop working when their end date or owner lapses, with the checks recorded

M26.2.5.why: Merged into M16.4.4, which asks for the same outcome: Entitlement expiry: memories stop matching when capabilities change. Owner approved merging duplicates on 2026-09-17.

M26.1.1.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 1 (built and wired, install check missing): Provisioning is done by the scheduled staff sync (ops.staff_sync_run via schedule_runner, staff_accounts_run makes accounts, staff_people_run writes members), not by identity.lifecycle.provision (no caller). Staff sources screen and routes; tests test_staff_sync_routes. Checks name M1.6.x only. NEXT: Write check naming M26.1.1 that runs a sync over a seeded roster and reads the new principal and its account row (reuse acceptance_checks_accounts.py harness).

M26.1.2.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 1 (built and wired, install check missing): ops.starter_pack_store.grant_starter_packs is called by staff_sync_run and gives each joiner the Starter pack for their department (decided needs 105); role from directory groups via identity.group_sync. Tests test_starter_pack_sync. Check M1.6.20/21 touches the step. NEXT: Add M26.1.2 to the leaves of the accounts check that covers the Starter pack step (acceptance_checks_accounts.py:420) or write one reading the grant.

M26.1.3.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 1 (built and wired, install check missing): starter_pack_sync.starter_plan scopes the pack to the person's registered department (department_scope), applied by starter_pack_store from staff_sync_run; a mover has it moved, a leaver has it ended. Test test_starter_pack_sync. NEXT: Check naming M26.1.3 that syncs a person into a department and reads the grant's scope; reuse the accounts check harness.

M26.1.4.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 3 (built, not wired): identity.lifecycle.welcome_questions and adoption.starter_questions (three department-scoped questions) are built; only ops.guide_docs imports the latter and nothing imports guide_docs. Ask.tsx says it suggests no question before the first ask. NEXT: Serve welcome_questions from a route for the signed-in person's department, from entities that indexed, and show them on the first Ask screen (Ask.tsx empty state).

M26.2.1.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 1 (built and wired, install check missing): Grants are read per request (gate.held_grants, disabled principal counts none) and the cache key carries the entitlement hash, so a move shows on the next request; existing check M6.5.2 (acceptance_checks_cache.py:116) shows a moved person is not served the old answer. lifecycle.Move is unwired. NEXT: Add M26.2.1 to the leaves of that M6.5.2 check, or write a check that moves a person and asks at once.

M26.2.2.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 2 (partly built): Personal agents follow the person by construction: E_run is the caller's reach intersected with the agent ceiling (gate.leash.decide), so a moved owner's agent reaches the new department. lifecycle.agents_following has no caller. Not verified that a personal agent's audience record updates on a move. NEXT: Check naming M26.2.2: move an owner, call their personal agent, assert old-department knowledge is not reached; fix the agent audience if it fails.

M26.2.3.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 3 (built, not wired): identity.lifecycle.reevaluate_delegations (suspend, never narrow) and Reconfirmation are built and tested but no caller; no delegation table or route exists on main (grep delegation in tables and routes). Nearest live object is an automation owner (M26.3.3). NEXT: Decide what a delegation is on this install (elevation, automation owner or a new object), then call reevaluate_delegations from the sync run when a move changes reach.

M26.2.4.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 1 (built and wired, install check missing): Answer cache key includes the entitlement hash (gate.answer_cache, cache_key); check M6.5.2 shows a person who moved department was refused the cached answer (acceptance_checks_cache.py:196). Test test_answer_cache. NEXT: Add M26.2.4 to that check's leaves=(...).

M26.2.6.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 1 (built and wired, install check missing): Knowledge reach is applied at query time from the reader's grants (knowledge.search scope, starter_pack_sync moves the pack with the person); nothing reindexes on a move. Test test_starter_pack_sync and knowledge scope tests. NEXT: Check naming M26.2.6: move a person between departments with no reindex job and assert search results change; reuse the people and knowledge check helpers.

M26.2.7.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 5 (not code, owner or blocked): Roll-up test leaf: tests/unit/test_lifecycle.py covers the pure module, but several clauses it covers (provision, delegations, welcome) are not wired, so a test of every item above has nothing end to end to run.

M26.3.1.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 1 (built and wired, install check missing): POST /govern/people/disable (principal_state_routes) sets disabled_at; migration 0003's trigger ends every session and grants go inert; the staff sync disables leavers via ops.standing_run (check M1.6.14). identity.lifecycle.disable is the unwired in-memory twin. NEXT: Write check naming M26.3.1: disable a signed-in person, assert the next request is refused and the session row ended (acceptance_checks_accounts.py has the harness).

M26.3.2.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 1 (built and wired, install check missing): ops.staff_sync_run calls stop_leavers_agents in the leaver's run (M1.8.9); staff_source_routes lists agents_for_adoption and adopt; Transfers.tsx page; tests test_staff_connect, test_staff_sync_routes. Adoption is by the department admin. NEXT: Write check naming M26.3.2: mark a leaver with an agent, assert the agent is disabled and appears in transfers, adopt it.

M26.3.3.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 1 (built and wired, install check missing): ops.automation_owner.standing_of returns AWAITING_OWNER when the owner is not active; automation_run_store.owner_live refuses an owner_gone run; automations_routes may_adopt lets a new owner take it. Check M32.6 covers other clauses. NEXT: Write check naming M26.3.3: disable the owner of a seeded automation, assert it does not run and is listed as awaiting an owner.

M26.3.4.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 3 (built, not wired): identity.lifecycle.departure_disposition (per Store) and member_activity.DeletionRoute are built but have no route or job caller; nothing applies a leaver's memory or personal knowledge disposition when the sync marks them. NEXT: Call departure_disposition from the leaver step of staff_sync_run and record each disposition; surface it on the Transfers page.

M26.4.1.why: TRIAGE 2026-10-13 class 2 (partly built): Roll-up proof (a check can be written once clauses exist) across joiner, mover and leaver; clauses depend on unwired parts (delegations M26.2.3, personal knowledge disposition M26.3.4, ended grant mid-run, external person end date). NEXT: Waits on M26.2.3 and M26.3.4, then a person runs it and the checks are recorded.

modules.name: Console, reports, observability
leaf_texts: Trace id minted at ingress before identify
Metadata ledger with no content, long retention
Payload store with a separate role and an audit row before every read
Client-side masking before any span leaves the process

Per-request fields: principal, agent version, policy epoch, entitlement hash, lane, model, provider, time to first token, tokens in and out, tool count and latency, connector, cache hit, redaction count, fallback count, retry count, status
Traffic class declared at ingress with no default
Company overview, the landing screen with honest counting
Live runs
Model matrix and provider health
Connector health
Knowledge coverage and staleness
Queue and automations
Incidents: what is degraded now and what it blocks
The stop button, and everything currently stopped
People and grants
Scopes and departments
Roles: the six, what each is for, and who holds it
Capability catalogue: everything that can be granted at all
Staff sources: where the staff list is linked from and what each may assert
Access review: each department admin recertifies what their people hold
Approvals queue: what is waiting on a human
Sessions, with a control to end one, because revoking a grant does not close a session
Exports: what left the building and who took it
Retention and erasure, with the deletion queue
Access friction: where people repeatedly hit a boundary, by shape and never by name
Agents and leash state with promotion and demotion history
Skills and templates with the review queue
Knowledge library across every department, with per-item visibility scope
Learning review across every department, tiers separated and tier one undoable
Artifacts produced, with provenance and retention
Memory viewer with change history
Audit
Questions and gaps
Usage and tokens by person, department, model and agent
Budgets and spend limits, and what happens at the ceiling
Quality and canaries
Console reads are tool calls with required capabilities
Console rows entity-tagged so the redactor applies to reports
Report audience intersected with the caller's scope, never unioned
Three planes of visibility: existence, configuration, content
Super Admin self-grant writes a loud audit event and notifies the steward
Navigation computed from grants and never from a role
No count of the screens, rows or filter options withheld from a caller
Filter option lists intersected with the caller reach, because a dropdown is a listing
Every screen narrowable by department and by person, one filter shape for all of them
Screens whose subject is the installation are not offered at department scope
This install: release, migration level, profile and the features it turns on
Backup, last verified restore and the recovery drill
Rate limits and what is currently being throttled
Capacity: connections, memory and pool sizes against what is deployed
Every console read module has a screen in the browser or a written reason it has none, listed on every run, because a read nobody can open is a screen nobody has
Staff source: choose it, configure it and try it before it runs
People: who is here, what each holds, and the reach that follows from it
Departments and teams, and who belongs to each
Roles: the six, what each is for, and who holds it
The capability catalogue: everything that can be granted at all
Granting and removing a capability, at the scope the grantor holds and never wider
Elevation requests: who asked for more, what they were given, and when it lapses
Access review: each department lead recertifies what their people hold
Sessions, with a control to end one, because revoking a grant does not close a session
Sign-in links: which Keycloak subject is bound to which person, and unbinding one
Subscribers and notifications: who is told what, and how to stop it
The audit ledger, readable by an auditor and narrowable without naming what is withheld
Usage and tokens by person, department, model and agent
Spend, budgets and what happens at the ceiling
Service levels: what was promised, what was measured, and where the gap is
Adoption: who is using this, for what, and who has stopped

Questions and gaps: the questions no connected source or knowledge could answer, including those answered with nothing found, by department and the source or knowledge that would have, shown only to people who administer that department
Quality and the permission canaries
Knowledge library across every department, with per-item visibility scope
Learning review across every department, tiers separated and tier one undoable
Memory viewer with change history
Artifacts produced, with provenance and retention
Exports, retention and erasure, with the deletion queue
This install: release, migration level, profile and whether a newer release exists
Backup, last verified restore and the recovery drill
Rate limits and capacity: what is throttled now, and connections, memory and pools against what is deployed
My own things: what a person has asked, kept and been given, for a reader who administers nothing
The same screens at department scope, proved by a department-scoped person opening them and seeing less, with no screen whose subject is the installation offered at all

The audit docs/admin-console.md asks for: every thing an administrator would need to manage, read out of the schema, the modules, the routes and the settings, compared screen by screen against what the console serves, and each gap built or recorded with its reason
Navigation grouped by what an administrator is trying to do rather than by the module that serves it
Loading, empty, unreachable and failed are four different sentences on every screen, never one blank panel
A destructive action is confirmed, and the confirmation says what will happen and to what
Validation before the write, and an error that says what to do about it
Long lists page, search, filter and sort, with bulk actions wherever they are safe
A credential is written once and never read back, proved by a test that no response and no log line carries one
AI providers, models and the routing between them, managed from the console
Prompts and system instructions, managed from the console
Feature and module enablement, managed from the console
Notifications and email, managed from the console
Webhooks, managed from the console
Scheduled jobs and background work, seen and controlled from the console
Logs and errors, readable from the console without a shell on the server
File and object storage, managed from the console
Import and export, from the console
Every control is proved to reach the system: the write is followed to the row, to the audit entry it leaves, and to the behaviour it changes
A sign-in with a second factor is reported in the token the realm mints, so an administrator can use the admin and approve verbs at all
A sign-in without a second factor is told in words which of its own verbs it cannot use here and how to sign in again, and no refusal about data changes wording
Approvals are stored on a running install, and each decision leaves one ledger entry that survives a restart
The first administrator can open the Routing and Classification screens, and the audit export carries what the exporter may read with no count of the rest
A set-up install is furnished once with the capability registry, starter packs, a company-wide scope and signed built-in templates, and never with a person or a demo row
Every failure a console request can meet answers with a sentence the screen shows: no plain-text 500, no message-less 422, and a switched-off feature names its switch
The application role holds the privileges every console route's tables need, proved by an invariant over the routes rather than found on a server
Docstrings that describe a store or a route the code no longer matches are corrected, each behavioural correction with its test
The setup wizard names a data steward, who is granted each connected source's declared capabilities, so data access begins with a named, audited person and never with the administrator by default
Navigation in the module groups of docs/admin-console-architecture.md, served by the API from the screen registry, with the design of record updated first

Shared parts every page is built from, taken from shadcn/ui on Radix with Tailwind (the owner chose it on 2026-09-17) and themed with the Verz palette: sidebar, header, breadcrumbs, list page, detail page, tabs, drawer, toasts, empty, loading and failed states, bulk bar and write-once secret field
One server list contract for every long list: cursor, search, filters offered from the reader's own reach, declared sorts, and never a total
The theme follows docs/screens.html, with the accent read from the install's configuration and its text colour chosen for contrast in both themes
Global search over each module's own read, where no match and not permitted are one answer
A browser end-to-end harness in CI against a furnished install with a second-factor user, and a page object per module
Departments, teams and scopes created, renamed and retired from the console, each change audited
People: grant expiry, bulk grants, pack assignment, a leaver disabled with the adoption plan, reinstatement and ownership transfer
Roles appointed over a scope and packs assigned, with an Access view explaining who can reach what and why
Sign-in, identity provider, staff source and the directory sync managed from the console
Service accounts and API keys created, shown once, rotated and revoked
Agents created from a template or from scratch through saved drafts, a rehearsal and a publish a second person approves, then enabled, disabled, archived, duplicated and handed over
Agent templates installed, authored from an agent through the leak scan, and withdrawn
Skills retired, detached, searched and filtered, with current assignments and a check of their tools against the agent's ceiling before the write
Connectors: available and connected kept apart, key replaced, configuration edited as one change, and drift from the declaration shown
A credentials screen over the write-once credential routes

The agent page has three views, Dashboard, Profile and About, in that order with Dashboard first, under one header carrying spend this period linked to Usage, the skill count and the days since the agent was created
The agent Profile lists its connected sources, pinned skills and channels, each with add and remove and an overflow list, and says plainly where an assigned skill does not yet change a run
The agent Profile shows who can find and use the agent, its owner, departments and people, with add and remove
The agent Profile carries the memory and learning switch and the browsing switch, and shows no switch for a capability the product does not have, such as computer use

The agent Profile shows what the reference page does not: the autonomy level, what the agent may reach in plain words, the model tier, owner, template and version, enabled or disabled, approvals waiting, automations and history

The agent About view is an overview anybody can read: what the agent is for and who it helps, how it works as a flow from what starts it through what it reads, what it does, where a person approves and where the result goes, and what it will never do, each step derived from its channels, automations, ceiling, tools and leash so the flow cannot describe something the agent is not set up to do
An agent's run reads its assigned skills and its model tier
Connected sources are probed and read on a schedule, with health recorded and shown
Installed automations run, and are paused, resumed, changed and removed from the console
The stop button halts the install from the console and the halt survives a restart
Model calls are metered into spend, budgets are versioned from the console, and stops in force are visible
The leash suspends an action for an approver in reach, who decides it once
Settings edited from the console after setup, with a notice where a change needs a restart
A leash lowered at once and raised only with evidence and a named approver, with the history of both
Channels bound and verified from the console
System health and alerting over readiness, the worker, the vault, object storage, the identity provider and the breakers
The queue and side effects: unknown states resolved and dead letters redriven from the console
Import from the console: knowledge upload, a skill from a repository, a template document
Backup drills started and recorded from the console
The access friction digest and the canary findings shown
Handover and export sets beyond the audit trail

Home and People and access proved in the browser: list, search, filter, view, create, edit, verify, retire, reinstate, import and export where each applies, with validation, duplicate, permission, session, empty, loading, failure, confirmation, phone-width and audit cases
Agents and AI proved in the browser by the same cases
Knowledge and data proved in the browser by the same cases
Channels and notifications proved in the browser by the same cases
Operations proved in the browser by the same cases
Governance proved in the browser by the same cases
Reports proved in the browser by the same cases
Platform proved in the browser by the same cases, at company scope only

Opening the content of another department's item is a capability separate from seeing it in the inventory, revocable from the console, and every opening writes an audit entry naming the item and the reader
A department admin halts every agent run, automation and delegated run in their own department from the console at once, the halt survives a restart, and nothing outside that department stops

Roles and administration are proved on an install: a Super Admin without a grant sees an item exists but no content, granting themselves a capability writes a loud audit entry and notifies the steward, revoking the last two Super Admins is refused, a deputy lapses on its date and cannot appoint another, the setup names a data steward who grants the first staff their reads, every console write leaves a ledger entry with the writer's real reach and trace, and the who-can-access view matches what each person actually reaches, with the checks recorded
A person signing in with an account bound to nobody is told once that an administrator must link their account and who can, and the console does not sign them in again in a loop
The people screen shows under each person the agents they steward, so a leaver's agents are visible before the account is disabled
Each answer records reasoning tokens separately from output tokens and the time spent in each gate stage, so the latency and cost split can be read from the ledger per lane

An administrator sees every registered tool with its required capability and side-effect class in the console and can switch a tool off for the install, which removes it from every agent's catalogue at once
An administrator tests a connector from the console, and the test makes one probe under the connector's throttle, records the result on its health and returns no business rows
The skills screen shows on each skill how many runs invoked it in the chosen period, counted from run traces the reader may see and never from the assignment list
Stopping takes one action with no confirmation, resuming requires a written reason and says when the person resuming is not the person who stopped it, and a halt has no expiry

A question answered with nothing found is shown to a knowledge owner only when the owner's own reach covers everything the asker's reach covers and the owner's search also finds nothing, so a gap in company knowledge is visible without telling anybody what an asker was refused
Every console requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves
Two console tabs open on one session refresh it without signing either out, proved in the browser
The Stop control is in the header of every console page for a reader who holds the halt capability, and absent for everybody else.
Resuming a halt is refused without a stated reason, the resume names the halt it overrides, and a halt whose state cannot be read is treated as in force.
A halt on one department or one person refuses that department's or that person's new work, and each stop axis the admission path does not yet enforce is named on the Stop screen.

The dashboard lists each waiting queue the reader could open (approvals, access review, elevation, skill reviews, tier-three learning, publish approvals, unbound sign-ins, knowledge past review), filters by period and department, and withholds any figure whose screen the reader cannot open.
A person's page lists the agents and automations they own and the ledger entries about them, each entry shown only to a reader who may read it.
An administrator creates a person by hand from the console on an install with no staff source, and that person can then be linked to a sign-in, placed in a department and granted
Removing a single capability a person holds through a pack is refused with a sentence naming the pack.
The people list, the department and team structure and an access certification report each export from the console, carrying only rows the exporter may read and no count of the rest.
Retiring a department with live grants bounded by its scope is refused until they move, and a department created from the console is grantable in the same session.

A department page shows members, lead history, its scope as a sentence, agents addressed to it and knowledge coverage, and applying the staff source's organisation plan creates the departments and teams it names.
A pack is created, versioned, copied and retired from the console, each write confirmed and audited, and assigning a pack widens a person by exactly that pack.
Every session of one person ends in one confirmed act, and a sign-in unlinked by mistake is re-linked to the same person with both acts in the ledger.
A service account runs at its owner's live reach narrowed by its ceiling, holds at most two live keys, can never carry approve or admin, and its owner and expiry change from the console.
Every run records the agent it ran as, so the agents list shows runs and cost per agent and the agent Dashboard lists its recent runs.
An agent's effective manifest exports as a document without company values, and importing one runs the leak scan and lands as a draft.
Publish, enable, disable, archive, transfer and every leash move write a ledger entry, and the audit log filters by agent id.

Approval cards carry the agent that raised them and filter by agent, and an agent's Dashboard shows only the cards the reader could decide, absent rather than nought for a reader who could decide none.
A widened publish appears in the Approvals queue for a second person who is not its author, and approving it publishes the agent.
The agent Profile offers computer use only once an isolated desktop runner exists, and says in a sentence that it is not offered until then.
Every money figure the API returns carries the install currency, and a spend figure with no metering behind it is served as not recorded rather than zero.
The memory and artifact reads filter by agent, and the agent's tabs show only what the reader may see.
Withdrawing a template version and undoing it are insert-only and audited, installed agents stay pinned, and a template exports as a signed document another install imports.
A Tools tab lists every registered tool with its required capability, side effect and source.
An administrator adopts an ownerless automation, which then runs as the adopter, audited.
A rung is added, retired or moved from the console as a new position row, audited, and the routing configuration exports without keys.
A connection record exports with its declaration and history and no credential.
Verify, review date, supersede, archive and bulk re-verify are console writes on a knowledge item, each audited, and widening its visibility waits for a holder of the visibility approval.
A reviewed classification is applied by a person other than its proposer, fast-path rules are listed, and pending entity merges are approved or rejected from the console.
Every artifact download is checked against the requester's current reach and leaves an audit entry.
Each channel shows the verbs it may carry and its rooms at their floor, and switching it off refuses its inbound messages.
A webhook is switched back on as a recorded change, and an exhausted delivery is replayed from the console once, audited.
Acknowledging an alert records who and when and stops its repeat notice, and the incident screen is offered at company scope only.
Runs and queue lists live runs by state, and resolving an unknown side effect asks for confirmation naming the operation.
Each background job lists its past runs, says when nothing runs it, and keeps a pause across a restart.
Logs and each report export from their screens with only rows the exporter may read and no count of the rest.
A settings write needs the settings admin capability, an identity provider change updates its redirect addresses, and the embedding size cannot change once content is embedded.
Every vault slot is written from the credentials screen, which shows an outranking environment variable and the vault state without any value.
The release check is a console setting as well as an environment value.
Every destructive control names its act (retire, end, disconnect, switch off, withdraw, detach, supersede), and a table outside the designed hard deletes grants the application no delete.
A browser check finds no task id, route path or internal constant in any page's visible text, and every not-yet-available control is disabled with a plain-words reason.
Every console screen that reports a guarantee as held reads the state of the control that keeps it, and shows the guarantee as not held while that control is unreachable, never run or behind
Detaching, retiring and reinstating a skill each add a record and never change or remove one, and the current assignments are derived from the absence of a later detachment or replacement
Assigning a retired skill is refused, and retiring a skill lists every agent still holding it for detachment without detaching any of them
Until a skill can be imported from a repository, the import screen says why only upload and paste are offered
A connector's page lists the agents whose manifest names the source and the skills whose tools come from it, narrowed to what the reader may see
Test connection on a connector's page runs one throttled probe, records it, and shows success or failure without any business record
The Access tab shows a person which of their own actions need a stronger sign-in, and shows an administrator viewing another person only the assurance each console action needs
A person's Access tab previews, for a chosen agent, what a run through that agent would reach for that person, computed by the gate itself
The console offers who-can-reach questions only for a capability over a scope, and no screen or route answers who can see a named record
No console screen states why a record was withheld, and filter choices never include a department the reader cannot reach
The console frame shows no count badge on any menu entry; counts appear only on the Dashboard, each governed by its own permission
At phone width a visible Menu button precedes the page content, opens every group, reaches every entry and returns focus when closed
The console header shows the signed-in person's sign-in strength and offers signing in again with an authenticator when it is not strong
Each tab of a detail page has its own address that opens that tab directly and survives a reload
Template install and the first run of a new install are stepped wizards whose draft survives leaving the page
Every empty list says what would add a row and which role may add it
Every action the install cannot yet perform, or the reader cannot perform here, is explained by a sentence the server serves, rendered by one component
Buttons carry primary, quiet and danger variants, and the Dashboard shows KPI tiles, a Needs-you list and an activity feed in headed cards
Every class in the console's markup has a style rule and every page reports a failure through the shared failure component, checked in CI

The shared parts and every restyled page pass the boundary check, the destructive-confirmed, validated-before-write, long-lists and screen-states tests, each changed only in the same commit that states its replacement property
The initial console bundle excludes the data table, form libraries, command palette and toaster, proved by the bundle-split test
The console's fonts are served from the install itself, and loading any page makes no request to a font host
A colour class that names no token fails the boundary check, and Tailwind's default palette is absent from the build
Old console stylesheets sit in a legacy cascade layer that no new component is overridden by, and a page leaves it only with its module's package
The boundary check refuses any cookie write in the console, and a selection checkbox shows indeterminate when only some rows are selected
Every console dependency's licence is on an allowed list checked in CI
The commit that restyles the first page keeps the phone-width, status-primitive and theme guarantees by testing the compiled CSS or the browser
The console's content security policy for styles is stated and the toaster and dialogs work under it
Using any console page makes no request to any host other than the install itself
The reference screenshots are held in the docs and each console page they cover records what was adapted and what was refused
Every console page is rebuilt on the shared shadcn/ui parts to the key screens design in docs/screens.html or better, one page at a time, and /build lists which pages are rebuilt

A console-wide clean-up removes what an administrator does not need, such as internal ids in page text, developer wording, duplicate panels and controls that explain the implementation, and records each removal with its reason

Every list page offers the management tools an enterprise console has: bulk actions over a selection, export of what the reader may see, saved filters, column choice and a detail drawer, with DENIED and ABSENT kept indistinguishable
The key screens page shows one designed screen for each primary page, the agent detail page included, and no page is rebuilt before its screen is there
A page counts as rebuilt only after a browser walk-through of it passes on the owner's install

M27.11.12.why: built (M27/agent-profile-and-personal-agents): an agent's Profile lists its sources, its skills and its channels each with its state. A channel is drawn as on or as off in words and a dashed edge (AgentChannels, from the lifecycle read), a source is attached or requested with the Connectors page's health, and a skill is drawn with its review and its runs. A skill no run of the agent could use says so in a sentence from the API (brain.console.agent_behaviour.skill_standing: not in the library, waiting for review, rejected, changed since it was approved, or naming a tool the agent may not call), checked against the run path's own skills_offered; the old sentence that an assignment changes no answer was false since M27.12.1 and is gone. Skills and channels hold the same overflow list as sources, the first five and the rest behind N more. Add and remove: a skill is attached and taken off through a confirmation, a source through a draft of the agent, a channel through the Change where it answers confirmation. Install check a_pinned_skill_no_run_could_use_is_said_so_on_the_profile. To prove on the install: sign in as an administrator, open an agent's Profile; the Capabilities card lists its skills, and under them a line for any skill no run uses, for example a skill still waiting for review; the card Where it answers shows each channel as on or as off

A reader who answers for the agent in no way is sent no name and no sentence saying names exist, so an agent offered to nobody and to many read the same; a personal agent takes no offer; the row stays on withdrawal with who and when. Backups are proved on an install: a copy lands off-host with its manifest every night for seven consecutive nights, a missed night raises an alert a person receives, the last verified restore reads never verified until a drill restores a copy and checks its schema, row-level security and permissions as well as its row counts, and no copy older than the erasure horizon remains, with the checks recorded

Operations are proved on an install: the service levels screen shows each lane's measured p50 and p95, permission and redaction latency and success rate beside its target, computed from the ledger and naming the connector timeout in force, and a scheduled control that misses its window and a backup older than its recovery point each raise an alert, and stopping the worker and failing a permission canary each deliver an alert to the named on-call person within its window, with the checks recorded

The company sets its own time targets in seconds for first output and for a complete answer in each lane before go-live, and they are recorded as the targets the service levels screen measures against
Enabling an edge proxy or tunnel on an install that declares a residency constraint states that encryption then ends at the provider's edge and requires an administrator to record acceptance first
An install on a profile with a recovery point under four hours replicates its object store off the host and has a standby database it fails over to in a recorded drill before that profile is offered
The service level statement is produced only after a restore drill verified a copy and the newest copy is inside the promised recovery point, and otherwise it is refused with the reason

Recovery and resilience are proved on an install: backups land off the host encrypted with the client's key, a restore drill is timed against the profile's recovery targets, a worker killed mid-task recovers without repeating its action, the chaos suite runs, and the capacity profile and scaling trigger measurements are read back from the running install, with the checks recorded

modules.name: Application scaffold and runtime
leaf_texts: App factory with settings injection
Lifespan startup: database pool, Valkey, OpenBao client, model registry
Lifespan shutdown with graceful drain
Health endpoint separating liveness from readiness
Readiness gated on database, cache and secret store all reachable
Uvicorn worker configuration per profile
Graceful shutdown honouring in-flight requests
Signal handling for container stop
Request timeout middleware distinct from the model timeout
Correlation id assignment before anything else
Structured logging with the trace id on every line
Exception handler mapping the error taxonomy to responses
CORS policy for the console and widget only
Security headers
Versioned route prefix and deprecation policy
OpenAPI generation with auth documented
Error response schema shared across every endpoint
Pagination convention applied uniformly
Declarative base with naming convention
Session management per request and per job
Async engine configuration against PgBouncer transaction mode
Separate session-mode engine for the worker
Model mixins: timestamps, soft delete, audit fields
Alembic environment reading settings, not hardcoded URLs
Autogenerate review rule: never merge an unreviewed autogenerated migration
Backward-compatibility test for one release
Data migrations separated from schema migrations
Migration run order at deploy, before traffic
Pydantic settings with per-environment overlays
Every variable documented in the example file
Fail-fast on a missing required variable at startup
Config as data in Postgres for anything an operator tunes
Deployment and unseal procedure documented for the client
Policy per role: application, worker, browser runner
Dynamic lease issuance for connector credentials
Lease revocation on run end
Rotation without redeploy
Audit device enabled and shipped to the ledger
Readiness reports sign-in as its own part, true only when the configured identity provider issuer answers, and a wrong issuer leaves the site up with sign-in refused and named as not ready
The application connects with a login that is not a superuser and cannot bypass row-level security, only migrations run as the owner, and a test fails if a request transaction can run as the owner

An approval, in the console or on a chat card, is rendered at the approver's own reach, carries no value from the requester's data, shows locked any field the approver could not look up, and refuses a press from anyone other than the person it was rendered for

Installer access and secrets are proved on an install: the installing partner holds no reach, opens a break-glass session with a stated reason that expires on its own, lands on its own audit chain and is notified to the company, the vault opens only with three of five shares with its root token revoked, and an API key is shown once, rotated and revoked without ever being displayed again, with the checks recorded
Installing, enabling or removing a connector needs a capability of its own that a department admin cannot grant wider than their department, and the refusal names that capability

modules.name: Migration, launch and handover
leaf_texts: Catalogue what the current Company Brain holds: knowledge, prompts, tool definitions, conversation history
Decide per item: migrate, rebuild or retire
Map old permissions onto the new capability model, explicitly rather than by assumption
Knowledge and asset export from the old system
Re-parse and re-embed rather than copying vectors, since embeddings are model-specific
Entity registry seeded from existing client records
Historical conversations archived, not imported, unless there is a stated reason
Both systems answering the same questions for an agreed period
Answer comparison log with disagreements surfaced
Cutover criteria agreed in writing before the period starts
Old system read-only, then archived
Credential revocation on every connector the old system held
Scheduled jobs disabled and verified stopped
Final backup retained per the retention policy
Inventory the twelve house skills, named individually, since each is authored work and not a setting
Inventory every agent with its connectors, skills, channels and availability, because an agent is a composition and not a prompt
Inventory automations, which are owned by an agent there and will be owned by an agent here
Export memory files, both curated and chat-extracted, with their change history
List which Lark groups each agent is installed into, since that is what staff actually see
Record what AnyGen produced that anyone still relies on
Export verz-master-theme, verz-doc-letterhead, seo-audit and website-cro-audit first: they are in daily use and are the test of whether import works at all
Convert the description convention, since theirs are written as router prompts beginning "Use the X skill to"
Re-review every imported skill through the normal queue rather than trusting it because it worked before
Diff behaviour on a real task before and after import, not just that the file parses
Retire any skill that has not been invoked in ninety days rather than carrying it over
Rebuild each agent from a template rather than importing its configuration, because their model has no ceiling and no leash to carry across
Set an explicit ceiling per agent, which AnyGen never had
Start every rebuilt agent at Shadow on writes regardless of how it behaved there
Map their Availability onto our availability, and their absent authority onto our entitlement, separately - conflating the two is the mistake their model makes
Their learning is one toggle over an opaque store; ours is four tiers with a review queue, and there is no honest mapping between them
Read the memory files as evidence and re-derive tier one preferences rather than importing beliefs wholesale
Discard anything that would widen a scope, since it was never approved by anyone under our rules
State plainly in the handover that the new system starts without their accumulated learning, and why that is the right trade
Install alongside, in one group first, with both bots present
Agreed period answering the same questions from both, with disagreements logged
Announce the switch before removing their bot, not after
Remove the AnyGen bot from each group in the agreed order
Keep their bot reachable read-only for an agreed window in case something was missed
Revoke every OAuth grant AnyGen holds - Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Sheets, Docs and the rest - because cancelling a subscription does not revoke them
Remove the AnyGen app from the Lark tenant, not just from the groups
Export anything with retention value before the account closes, since access ends with billing
Cancel the subscription only after the export is verified restorable
Record the date access actually ended, which is a different date from the last invoice
One department, agreed scope, named champion
Twenty real questions as the acceptance set
Daily review of every answer for the first week
Explicit go or no-go decision with written criteria
Rollout order agreed with the client
Per-department onboarding session
Per-department starter questions and knowledge seeding
Adoption measured as real questions from real people, machine traffic excluded
Staff session: what it can see, how to ask, how to correct it
Admin session: console walkthrough, grants, leashes, review queues
Recorded and left with the client
Acceptance criteria signed before build, not after
Invariant suite green, evidenced
Restore drill executed in front of the client
Security review completed if the client requires one
Penetration test scheduled where contractually required
Data processing agreement
Service level statement with the RPO and RTO from the chosen profile
Support and escalation procedure
Subprocessor list covering every model provider used
Runbook per console screen
Incident playbook per failure mode
Named client owner for knowledge, grants and connectors
Scheduled job registry handed over with what each one guards
Thirty-day post-launch review booked at handover
Every scheduled control listed with what it guards
CI assertion that each control appears in the scheduler
Alert when a scheduled job has not run within its window
Explicit test that no safety mechanism lacks a caller
Alert routing and severity definitions
Runbook per alert
Escalation path to us where the client cannot resolve it
Measured spend against the projection after thirty days
Estimator correction from actuals
Budget thresholds retuned with real distribution rather than assumptions
Two-factor on the deployment control panel account, because its sign-in page answers from the internet and it holds every container, database and secret on the host
Delete the temporary identity provider administrator created at bootstrap, so an internet-facing admin sign-in is one account to guess rather than two
Decide whether the administrative consoles stay on public subdomains or move behind an SSH tunnel, and write down which and why
Rotate the identity provider's bootstrap administrator password once the account it created has been deleted
The company names its data steward on the people screen and the steward grants each pilot department's staff their starter reads, recorded in the audit trail
The company switches on a second sign-in factor for every account on the identity provider's admin console and every other administrative console of the install, and records that each one asks for it
The company's administrator creates the ticket desk and chat workspace credentials with the scopes the integration guide lists and enters them on the connectors screen, never in a file or a message
The company's workspace administrator installs the product's chat app with the scopes the channel guide lists, adds it to the pilot groups and creates the directory app the staff source signs in with
A migration cutover cannot be recorded complete while revoking the old system's authorisations, recording the date its access ended or the restore drill is unrecorded, and the refusal names which

A migration is rehearsed on a throwaway install: skills are imported and re-reviewed, agents are rebuilt from templates at Shadow with no learning carried, and the cutover is refused until every security act is recorded, with the checks recorded
Commission a penetration test of the owner's install before the first company data is connected, and record each finding with its fix or accepted risk
Every migration requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves

M37.2.1.1.why: the count and the names are one company's authored estate, and a product every client installs cannot hold them

M37.2.1.5.why: one company's chat groups, named. The register that holds the answer is generic; the answer is not

M37.2.1.6.why: names the outgoing vendor and what it made for one company

M37.2.2.1.why: four of one company's skills by name. `brain.migration.skills` is the generic half and is built

M37.2.5.4.why: a bot left in a group keeps receiving that group's messages. Removing the tenant installation is the authorisation half and this is the delivery half, and either one left undone leaves the outgoing vendor reading the client's internal chat

M37.2.6.1.why: every grant is a live credential on somebody else's service and cancelling the subscription does not withdraw one. This is how an outgoing vendor keeps reading a client's mail after everybody believes the account is closed

M37.2.6.2.why: a tenant installation is a tenant-level grant. Removing the app from every group removes what staff see and leaves the scopes it was installed with, which is the same failure as an unrevoked grant one layer up

M37.2.6.5.why: without it there is no evidence of when access ended, and the last invoice is the date everybody reaches for instead. It is the fact an incident review or an audit asks for, and it cannot be reconstructed afterwards

M37.4.1.3.why: a backup nobody has read back is a file, which is the refusal `brain.ops.recovery` already makes about the live system and `FinalBackup.verified` makes about the last copy of the old one. In front of the client is what makes it evidence rather than a claim, and the cutover is the last moment it can be asked for

M37.6.1.1.why: a public sign-in page is fine when a guessed or stolen password is not sufficient on its own, and this one is not a console among others: it is the control plane for every container on the host, including the identity provider's own database and every environment variable in it. One credential between the internet and all of that is the single largest exposure on the box, and the fix is an authenticator scan

M37.6.1.2.why: the same shape as the OAuth grants two groups up: a credential left behind after it has served its purpose, on a service reachable from outside. It is worse than an unused password because nothing about an unused admin account looks different on the day it is used

M37.6.1.4.why: conditional on the deletion above and much smaller once it is done: with the account gone the value signs into nothing. Not gated, for the reason the two conditional acceptance leaves are not gated either, and a gate that fires when it should not is a gate somebody switches off

M37.4.2.2.why: Merged into M30.5.4, which asks for the same outcome: RPO and RTO per profile written into the client agreement. Owner approved merging duplicates on 2026-09-17.

M37.4.3.1.why: Merged into M34.3.2.1, which asks for the same outcome: Runbook per console screen. Owner approved merging duplicates on 2026-09-17.

modules.name: Continuous delivery and live status
leaf_texts: Branch per track named for its module, so twelve concurrent tracks do not collide
Commit message convention carrying the task id, for example M3.2.1
Pre-push hook running lint, types and the invariant suite locally
Pull request template listing the task ids the branch closes
CODEOWNERS forcing review on the gate, the redactor and the catalogue projection
Actions workflow: lint, type check, unit tests, invariant suite, schema sweeps
Migration forward and rollback against a production-shaped snapshot
Container image build with the commit SHA as the tag
Image signing
Push to the registry
Coolify deployment triggered on every push to main
Migrations applied before the new image takes traffic
Health gate: readiness must pass before the old container stops
Automatic rollback if readiness fails within the window
Deployment record written to the deployment history with the SHA and the task ids in that release, kept apart from the permission audit trail and out of the compliance export
Local compose for development
Staging on the same server, separate compose project and database
Production, deployed on every push once staging has passed the same commit
Seed data in staging, never production data
Record the deployed commit at the end of each wave; release tags are cut only for client installs
Run the full invariant suite against staging
Deploy to production
Smoke test: one real question answered end to end by a real person
Restore drill from wave three onward
Wave report generated automatically from the closed task ids
W0: nothing user-facing, but the pipeline itself deploys and is provably working
W1: a person asks in the console and gets a permission-correct answer from seeded data
W2: a real question answered live in Lark from a connected source
W3: agents installed from templates, answering with knowledge and memory
W4: automations running, approvals landing in Lark
W5: real connector credentials wired, browser tasks, go-live
CI step parsing every commit message for task ids
Status file written to the repository on each merge to main
Task marked done only when its branch merges and CI is green, never by hand
Percentage, per-wave and per-module progress computed from that file
Status page served by the application itself at a fixed path
Reads the status file baked into the image at build time
Shows overall percentage, current wave, tasks closed today, and what is next
Shows the deployed commit SHA and when it shipped
Visible to the client so progress needs no meeting
Automated message to a Lark channel each evening
Tasks closed, tasks opened, anything overdue
Wave burn-down against the target date
Sent by the system itself once W2 has shipped the Lark channel
Every connector built and tested against recorded cassettes, so credentials never block development
Contract tests proving the adapter matches the recorded shape
Credential slots defined in OpenBao with the scopes each connector needs, empty until go-live
Obtain and store real credentials per connector
Replay the contract tests against the live API and diff against the cassette
Rate-limit ceilings confirmed against the live account tier, not the documentation
First sync run with the projection populated and verified
Cassettes refreshed from live so future development stays faithful
After each staging deploy the permission canaries and the row-level security sweep run against the staging database, and a failure stops the commit being promoted

CI scans the image and every locked dependency for known vulnerabilities on each build and fails on a critical finding without a recorded exception, and a written threat model of the install's exposed surfaces is kept beside the release

On the owner's install a Maintenance Agent assembled from the console answers a real maintenance question in Lark from uploaded maintenance knowledge and the ticket desk, runs one workflow that stops for one approval, and the run is signed off against acceptance criteria written before it

On the owner's install the task tracker, /build and status.json show Done, which has been shown working, beside Built, which is merged with CI passed and a test naming the task and not yet shown working, with a note in plain words and no built task counted as done, and the install proof sweep closes a task on one complete clean run, a run repeatable for only the checks that failed or came back not run

modules.name: Agent workspace, the inside-an-agent surface
leaf_texts: An agent record composes persona, knowledge scope, connectors, skills, tools, workflows, channels, availability, leash, model policy, memory and automations
Every attachment stored as a reference with a pinned version, never an inline copy
Attachment add and remove written to the ledger with who, when and why
Divergence flag when an instance edits something its template supplies
Composition diff between an instance and its template, rendered side by side
Agent header: avatar, name, role line, owner, template lineage and version
Tab strip: Conversations, Automations, People, Knowledge, Memory, Artifacts, Settings
Right pane switches between Dashboard and Profile without losing tab state
Deep link to any tab so a console alert can point at the exact place
Keyboard navigation across tabs and back to the roster
Spend, runs and messages as the agent's headline figures, not a buried report
Range selector across seven, thirty and ninety days and month to date
Cost attributed per caller so a single heavy user is visible
Projection to month end against the agent's own budget
Connector row with per-source icons and an overflow count
Attach and detach with the capability check performed at attach time
Each connector shows which fields it projects for this agent
A connector the agent asks for but the department has not granted shown as requested, not attached
Health inherited from the connector page so a degraded source is visible here
Skill chips with version, source and review state
Attach only from the approved library, never directly from a repository
Unapproved skill offered with a route to the review queue rather than an attach button
Per-skill invocation count so unused attachments can be pruned
Skill description convention enforced: the description is the router prompt
Knowledge scope expressed as a predicate, not a document list
Add by upload, by link extraction, or by widening the predicate
Preview of how many items the predicate currently matches
Coverage and staleness for exactly this agent's slice
Items the agent retrieved most and items it never touched
Channel row with per-channel enable
Channel capability intersected with the agent ceiling before it is offered
Per-channel rendering profile chosen automatically
Group installation where the channel supports it
Availability block: which users and departments can find and invoke this agent
Ceiling block: the widest entitlement any run of this agent may reach
Explicit copy stating that availability is discovery and never authority
Worked preview: pick a person, see exactly what their run of this agent would return
Preview computed by the real gate, never by a separate estimation path
Leash matrix per target and scope, read, draft and write on separate rungs
Promotion requires evidence: clean runs, agreement rate and a named approver
Demotion by circuit breaker shown with the metric that tripped it
Money and irreversibility boundaries pinned so a rung cannot rise without a second approver
History of every promotion and demotion with the evidence attached
Memory rendered as readable text, never an opaque store
Split between curated memory and memory extracted from conversations
Change history with a diff per revision and the trigger that caused it
Direct edit and direct delete by the owner
Per-agent and per-person memory shown separately so neither hides the other
Which tiers are active for this agent
Tier one changes listed with one-click undo, never an approval queue
Tier two rules shown with their shadow evidence and a promote control
Tier three items routed to the department queue with a link back here
A single control to freeze all learning for this agent during an incident
Every produced document, deck, report, export and image recorded as an artifact
Artifact carries producing run, agent version, caller, entitlement hash and timestamp
Stored in the object store with the retention class of its most sensitive input
Field-level redaction applied at production time, so an artifact never exceeds its caller
Re-download re-checks the requester entitlement rather than trusting the original link
Artifacts tab listing what this agent produced, newest first
Filter by type, by caller and by date
Provenance panel: which sources and which knowledge items fed it
Supersede and archive rather than delete
Artifact count and storage shown against the retention policy
Automations listed under the agent that owns them, never in a global pile
Named as outcomes in the first person, not as trigger and action mechanics
Template gallery for common automations with a one-step install
Per-automation run history with the last result and the next scheduled time
Pause, resume and delete with the scheduler registry updated in the same transaction
An automation runs on a named principal, never on the agent itself
Schedule changes are a tier three learning event and need a human
Failure after a threshold pauses the automation and notifies the owner
Every automation appears in the scheduled job registry with what it guards

An agent is configured with which kinds of memory it may read and write (the conversation, the task, the project, the person and its own), and a run cannot read a kind of memory its configuration leaves out

An agent is assembled on the install from console choices alone, picking knowledge, connectors, skills, channels, tools and workflows that were each created separately, and it answers through its assigned channel with no code change or release, proved on the install for a maintenance agent and an SEO agent

Changing an agent attachment is refused on the server unless the caller holds that attachment's editing role (owner for persona, knowledge, skills, memory and automations; department admin for connectors, channels, ceiling and leash; super admin for model policy), and the refusal names the role required

An agent's supervision pin is reviewed at thirty days against a confidence measured from its supervised runs, extends while that confidence is below 90 percent, ends only when a person confirms it at or above 90 percent, and never lapses because a date passed

The leash is proved on an install: the same agent action runs simulated and marked at Shadow, suspends at Assisted and proceeds at Autonomous only where no sensitive effect is declared, the strictest of overlapping rules wins, a department admin lowers a rung at once while raising one needs evidence and a named approver and two for a money boundary, a breaker demotes a rung showing the metric that tripped, and a supervision pin extends below its confidence bar, with the checks recorded

Artifacts are proved on an install: a report produced for one person holds only what that person may see, a re-download after their reach narrows is re-checked and refused, its retention follows its most sensitive input, and a new version supersedes rather than edits it, with the checks recorded
An artifact records the canonical client it was produced for, and an agent can retrieve the latest artifact of a given type for that client, re-checked against the asker's reach
The agent workspace lists the tools attached to an agent with add and remove, checks each against the agent's ceiling when it is attached, and a run's catalogue carries only attached tools

The maintenance agent runs end to end on the owner's install: a question in the chat channel is answered from uploaded maintenance knowledge and the ticket desk through its vault credential, its maintenance workflow runs on the worker, and one prepared action waits for and receives an approval on a chat card before it executes, with the checks recorded

Agent configuration is proved on an install: an agent is asked by a junior and a senior person, from an assigned and an unassigned channel, and is led toward an unassigned skill, tool, connector, workflow and memory kind and an action needing approval, and each is refused, narrowed or held for approval as its configuration says, with the checks recorded

The agent's Conversations section lists only threads the reader may see, filterable to threads the reader took part in, each showing participants, relative time, a preview and the run state including failed

The agent page has a Knowledge section among its tabs that lists what this agent draws on: each document or web page with its kind, title, where it came from, who added it and when, whether it is verified or due for review and whether this agent reaches it, with an empty state that says what the section is for and offers both ways to add, and it works at phone width

A person who may add knowledge uploads a file from their device in the agent's Knowledge section, through the same door as the Knowledge page (type proved from the bytes, size limit, scan), and is told in one sentence whether this agent reaches it

A person adds a web page in the agent's Knowledge section by giving its link, which is fetched once through the same checked door (private addresses refused) and kept as the company's own copy with a review date, and is told whether this agent reaches it

An item this agent does not reach says so beside it and offers the one next step, to widen what the agent draws on through a draft or to place it where the agent's rule already reaches, and nothing is added to every agent silently

A link added from the Knowledge section is fetched again only when a person asks, a file is replaced by a new version, and whoever may retire an item can take it away, after which the agent stops drawing on it at once

Every item the section shows is one its reader may read, an item the reader may not see is absent with no count of what is hidden, and what the agent draws on for a run is the intersection with the caller's own reach

The Knowledge section also lists the other sources the agent draws on, a connected source or a skill's references, each named by kind and linking to the page that owns it, so one place shows the agent's whole context

Proved on the install: a reserved person adds a file and a link from an agent's Knowledge section and is told whether the agent reaches each, a colleague without the grant sees neither, and the agent then answers from the file and cites it
Proved in the browser: the Knowledge section lists, adds by upload and by link, refuses a link to a private address and shows an unreached item with its next step, at desktop and phone widths

The agent's Automations section offers New automation, which starts from a named outcome template or a description in plain words and lets the person set what it does, when it runs and where its result goes, never a blank canvas of steps

A new automation's trigger is chosen as a schedule, a connector event or a webhook, with an optional condition from a short named list (for example only when an invoice is more than seven days overdue, never free code), and its card says both in words

What a new automation does is an instruction to this agent within its ceiling and leash, with the skills and tools it may use named on its card, and anything it would write waits for a person as every agent write does
A new automation is rehearsed before it is switched on, showing what it would have done at its owner's reach for the last few triggers while writing and sending nothing

Proved on the install: a reserved person creates an automation from a template with a changed trigger and condition, rehearses it, switches it on, and a run starts as that person and is held to their reach
Proved in the browser: New automation creates, rehearses and switches on an automation from the agent's Automations section, and a paused or suspended one says why, at desktop and phone widths

Every agent is either a team agent, which belongs to a department and is used by that department's people through the rule it carries, or a personal agent, which belongs to one person and is used only by them; the kind is chosen when the agent is created and shown on the agent's page

Any person may create a personal agent for themselves from the builder, within what their own reach allows and without anybody's approval to create it; a department administrator or a super administrator may create both kinds, and only they may create a team agent

A personal agent is listed, usable and visible only to its owner and, for oversight, to a reader who holds the audit capability for it, and what its owner connects to it is the owner's own and is never shared
A person connects their own Google account (mail, calendar, documents) to their personal agent and what it reads is that person's own, and no colleague, administrator or other agent can ask for it

A team agent never reads one person's mailbox for the team: team mail comes only from a shared mailbox an administrator connects, and a person's own mail reaches a team agent only inside that person's private conversation, never in a room, a memory or a knowledge item, as the owner decides in needs item 189

Proved on the install: a reserved person creates a personal agent that a colleague cannot see or ask, a department administrator creates a team agent, and a person without that capability is refused when trying to create one
Proved in the browser: the create flow offers the kind, shows a person who may only make their own the personal choice alone, and the agent's page names its kind, at desktop and phone widths

On an agent's page its steward and a holder of the lifecycle authority over it are also told that other people's conversations with it happened: who, when and whether the agent answered, declined or failed, and never the question or the answer, and a personal agent tells nobody but its owner anything

Proved on the install: an agent's steward is shown that a colleague's conversation with it happened, with who, when and that it failed, and no word the colleague asked or was answered; the colleague and a person who may not oversee the agent are shown none of it

Note for 210: an automation is admitted at read only (M39.6.2.1), so every tool it may name is a read tool; option A needs that admission to change first. modules.name: Member self-service application
leaf_texts: Single sign-on through Keycloak with the same identity the channels use
Channel identity and web identity resolved to one principal, never two
Session policy, idle timeout and device list
Password reset and recovery handled by the identity provider, not by us
Explicit test that a channel-only user can sign in and sees the same entitlement
Member navigation distinct from the admin console and much shorter
No administrative surface reachable by URL guessing, enforced server side
Responsive down to a phone since approvals arrive on phones
Entitlement disclosure line rendered from the real entitlement set, never hand-written
Questions asked this month with corrections separated out
Agents this person can call, split between department-provided and self-built
Personal budget consumed against the personal cap
Count of things learned about this person, each reversible
Recent threads continued from any channel, so web and Lark are one history
List with source, where each one runs and how often this person used it
Open an agent into the same workspace surface, bounded to what this person may see
Build a personal agent from a template within the person's own ceiling
Personal agent visible to nobody else unless explicitly shared
Request an agent the person cannot yet call, routed to the department admin
Items this person uploaded with visibility scope, verification date and review due
Upload, replace and retire with the review cycle set at upload time
Usage count so an author can see whether anything reads what they wrote
Request promotion to company-wide, routed as a tier three decision
Never shows an item outside this person's entitlement, including their own department's restricted rows
Personal skills with source, version and review state
Author in the studio, import from a repository or paste a URL
Submit to the department library for review
Personal skills usable only by this person's own agents until approved
Everything produced for this person by any agent
Re-download re-checked against current entitlement
Share with a colleague only where that colleague's entitlement already covers the contents
Plain-language list of every preference learned, with the evidence that produced it
One-click undo per item and an undo-all control
Weekly digest delivered in the person's own channel with the same controls
Opt out of personal learning entirely, with the cost stated honestly
What is stored about this person and where, in plain language
My conversation history with export
Deletion request routed to the retention policy rather than performed silently
Which agents have read my HR record, from the audit ledger
Personal account connections with per-source consent
Explicit copy stating that connecting an account never widens what the person may see
Disconnect with immediate token revocation
Department-provided connections shown as inherited and not disconnectable here
Which channels this person is reachable on and which is primary
Per-channel notification preferences
An approver's routing preference for envelope decisions chooses only between the console and a Lark card, never WhatsApp or email
Quiet hours honoured by automations and digests
Envelope approvals awaiting this person, with what will happen stated before the fact
Approve, reject and amend, each written to the ledger
Expiry on an unanswered approval with a stated default of doing nothing
Same approval reachable from Lark and from the web without double action
Mobile layout treated as the primary case for approvals

The mail relay configured at setup or on the notifications screen is also given to the identity provider, so a password reset email reaches the person on the install, and with no relay a forgotten-password link is not offered
A person can try an approved skill from its card, which opens a conversation with that skill pinned, run through the one agent runtime at the person's reach and metered like any other run
The web composer accepts an attached file and dictated speech, and dictation is transcribed through the registered speech tool at the person's reach before the text is sent

The member application is proved in the browser for a member who administers nothing: their agents, knowledge, skills, artifacts, memory, data, connected accounts and approvals, each showing only what that person may reach, with the checks recorded

The member application offers two starting points, start a task and talk to an agent, and a task started without an agent is routed by the gate to an agent the person may call, running at the person's reach
The member's recent tasks and threads each show their state, running, waiting for approval, done or failed, read from the job and suspension records, and a failed one says which step failed

A person can create a personal project grouping their threads and uploaded files, and a run inside it reads those files as project context at the person's reach on every turn, never storing them as memory
Opening an agent shows three starter prompts drawn from that agent's skills and the knowledge the person may reach, and never offers one the person's run could not answer

modules.name: Client independence, built in rather than stripped out
leaf_texts: Sweep refusing any client name, domain, work address, company id or storage path literal in src, migrations, console and compose
One settings module as the only place a client-specific value is read, so nothing reads the environment directly
Every client-specific value an environment variable with a declared default, a documented meaning and a refusal when it is missing
Branding as configuration: company name, logo, colours, product name, sender address
Identity provider as configuration: realm, issuer, client id, redirect URIs, brokered directory
Model and provider choice as configuration, including a local-only profile with no external provider
Storage, object store and vector store locations as configuration
The sweep runs in CI on every commit, so the final audit verifies a gate that has been green all along rather than cleaning a year of drift
Test: the application boots and answers a question configured as a fictitious company with no Verz value present
Migrations build every schema, table, index, constraint, trigger and row-level security policy from an empty database
Generic demo seed: a fictitious company, departments, people and records, deliberately not the Verz test fixture
No install step depends on a Verz database, dump, backup or export
First-run setup creating the first administrator, with no default password anywhere
CI job installing from empty into a scratch container and asking one question end to end
Uninstall and data-return procedure, because a client who leaves must be able to take their data and leave nothing behind
Starter pack loaded at install: the six roles, standard permission sets, the standard agents and sensible defaults, so a new client opens a furnished system rather than a blank one
Starter pack is separate from the demo seed, because a client wants the roles and not the fictitious records
The repository is the template and a client install is a release tag plus one environment file, so a fix reaches every client rather than one copy
No duplicated repository anywhere, because a copy diverges the first time a bug is fixed in one and not the other and nothing says so
Repository structure a reader can navigate: what is application, what is configured per client, what is never edited, where migrations, scripts and documentation live
Verz is one deployment: its values live in a per-install file and never in this repository

On a scratch install a handover exports every store and the audit ledger in open formats with a manifest the company can check, then removes the identity realm, bucket, vault secrets, schedules, route, containers and configuration, revokes connector authorisations and the chat app, and issues a certificate naming the date the last backup expires
